\chapter{Chapter05 — Random Boolean Fourier Maximum}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.RandomBooleanFourierMaximum}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Fourier infinity norm]
\lean{FABL.fourierInfinityNorm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p013-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b001
}
\label{FABL.fourierInfinityNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, define its Fourier
infinity norm to be the maximum, over all subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, of the
absolute value of its Fourier coefficient at $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Random Boolean Fourier threshold]
\lean{FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold}
\label{FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, define the random Boolean Fourier threshold to be $2\sqrt
n\,2^{-n/2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity sign]
\lean{FABL.paritySign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001
}
\label{FABL.paritySign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a point $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define the parity
sign on $S$ at $x$ to be the product of the coordinates $x_i$ for $i\in S$, regarded as
a unit in the integers.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$.
The real value of the sign obtained by multiplying the coordinates $x_i$ for $i\in S$
equals the monomial $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Multiplicativity of sign values]
\lean{FABL.signValue_mul}
\label{FABL.signValue_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
For any signs $a$ and $b$, the real value of their product is the product of their real
values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Random Boolean coefficient sample equivalence]
\lean{FABL.randomBooleanCoefficientSampleEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b001}
\label{FABL.randomBooleanCoefficientSampleEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign, FABL.paritySign}
For a natural number $n$ and a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, there is a bijection
from the Boolean functions on the $n$-dimensional cube with values in the two integer
units to functions from a set of size $2^n$ to the two integer units, obtained by
reindexing cube inputs and multiplying each output by the parity sign on $S$ at the
corresponding input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Empirical mean of a Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean_randomBooleanCoefficientSampleEquiv}
\label{FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean_randomBooleanCoefficientSampleEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.randomBooleanCoefficientSampleEquiv, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_mul, FABL.signValue_paritySign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S$ be a subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. The average, over all inputs $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, of
$f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the Fourier threshold]
\lean{FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold_nonneg}
\label{FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the quantity $2\sqrt{n}\,2^{-n/2}$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean Fourier threshold identity]
\lean{FABL.card_mul_randomBooleanFourierThreshold_sq_div_two}
\label{FABL.card_mul_randomBooleanFourierThreshold_sq_div_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, define $\tau_n=2\sqrt{n}\,2^{-n/2}$. Then the Boolean cube
$\{-1,1\}^n$ satisfies $|\{-1,1\}^n|\tau_n^2/2=2n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be any set of coordinate indices, and choose a
sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube uniformly at random. The
probability that the absolute value of its Fourier coefficient at $S$ is at least
$2\sqrt n\,2^{-n/2}$ is at most $2\exp(-2n)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Large Fourier maximum has a large coefficient]
\lean{FABL.randomBooleanFourierMaximumBad_subset}
\label{FABL.randomBooleanFourierMaximumBad_subset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierInfinityNorm, FABL.randomBooleanFourierThreshold}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Set
$T_n=2\sqrt{n}\,2^{-n/2}$. If the largest absolute value of a Fourier coefficient of $f$
exceeds $T_n$, then some Fourier coefficient has absolute value at least $T_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential bound]
\lean{FABL.two_pow_two_mul_add_one_lt_exp_two_mul}
\label{FABL.two_pow_two_mul_add_one_lt_exp_two_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For every integer $n\ge 2$, $2^{2n+1}<\exp(2n)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An exponential power bound]
\lean{FABL.two_pow_mul_two_exp_neg_two_mul_le_rpow_neg}
\label{FABL.two_pow_mul_two_exp_neg_two_mul_le_rpow_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.two_pow_two_mul_add_one_lt_exp_two_mul}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $n\ge 2$, $2^n\,2e^{-2n}\le 2^{-n}$.
\end{theorem}
